newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas falls again, March in contango to summer.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas falls again, March in contango to summer.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market closed lower again on Wednesday, with front month March well down, brokers said.
But trade was once again extremely thin with only 50 lots traded and deals only seen in two of the contract's 12 months, although this was up on Tuesday's volume.

March closed down 0.565 pence a therm at 10.795 pence, having hit a contract low of 10.70 pence earlier, against a high of 14.90 pence a therm. June, the other month traded, also down by 0.25 pence a therm at 11.10 pence.
The fall on March has twisted it into contango with the summer, unexpected given that gas use is so closely related to the weather and summer prices are traditionally lower than in winter.

"It's a shock to some people to see a winter price below a summer price," said a broker. "It's not gone down too well with some of them. People in this market are not used to contangos or backwardations."

He added that many still used futures much as they used the OTC market, and its prices were too closely tied to the physical market to allow the development of real trade. But he felt that trade would still pick up as more players got used to the new market.
